ClientResponses.Response:
We are sorry to hear about your disappointment with your grill. The issue you are describing inside your lid is not caused by paint, since Weber does not use paint inside our grill lids. What you are seeing is called "carbonized grease."
As you use your grill, vapors and grease from the grilling process can build up and create a deposit on the inside of your grill lid.

The high heat of the grill will cause the the deposit to harden, and it will begin to flake or peel off. This peeling or flaking substance will be paper thin, black, and glossy on one side and matte on the other.

This can be treated by cleaning the grill:
First, use a Weber stainless steel bristle brush and clean off as much of the build-up as you can. This should remove most of the accumulated carbonized grease.

Next, a plastic scraping tool can be used to clean any stubborn bits of carbonized grease that weren't removed by the brush.

For a deeper cleaning, after brushing and scraping the lid, spray it with the Weber Grill Grate Cleaner found in our cleaning kits, which will break down the remaining grease. Let the cleaner sit on the lid for about 30 seconds before wiping it with a damp paper towel. If you do not have the Weber Grill Grate Cleaner, you can use soap and water while the lid is warm, not hot. 

As for your Flavorizer bars, we also recommend cleaning those regularly to keep them lasting their longest. Once you have holes, though, it's time for a replacement. Your grill is backed by a generous warranty. Our Support team reached out via email to help get your replacement started and help with anything else that you may need. Thanks for your patience and for being a Weber fan!
